label: Crisp
terms_note: Automation allowed: base https://api.crisp.chat/v1/, HTTP Basic with identifier:key, X-Crisp-Tier: user | plugin (plugin tokens for marketplace plugins, user tokens for a workspace's own account). Rate limit referenced as 5 requests per second per token with tier-dependent quotas. Endpoints: GET /website/{website_id}/conversations/{page} (filters: inbox, unread, resolved, assigned, dates), GET /website/{website_id}/conversation/{session_id}, POST /website/{website_id}/conversation/{session_id}/message {type text|note|file|animation|audio|picker|field|carousel|event, from user|operator, origin chat|email|urn:*, content}. Inbound via RTM events (message:send, message:received, session state) or web hooks.

sdks: Official Crisp API wrappers (node-crisp-api, python-crisp-api, go-crisp-api, php-crisp-api, ruby-crisp-api) — docs.crisp.chat

reference.limits: - Documented as **5 requests per second per token**, quotas vary by tier; 429 on excess. Errors `{error: true, reason}`. - Plugin-tier tokens are for marketplace plugins; user-tier tokens operate the user's own workspace — no approval needed.

fields.name: identifier
fields.help: Identifier half of the Crisp token keypair (plugin token from the Marketplace, or a website token), sent as the HTTP Basic username — 'Authorization: Basic BASE64(identifier:key)' (https://docs.crisp.chat/guides/rest-api/authentication/plugin-token/, https://docs.crisp.chat/guides/rest-api/authentication/website-token/).

fields.name: key
fields.help: Key half of the Crisp token keypair, sent as the HTTP Basic password ('--user "{identifier}:{key}"' in the official curl examples).

adapter.headers_note: Crisp requires X-Crisp-Tier on every call; the static header is pinned to 'plugin' ('X-Crisp-Tier: plugin', the plugin-token guide). Website tokens are documented with 'X-Crisp-Tier: website' instead (https://docs.crisp.chat/guides/rest-api/authentication/website-token/); the runtime's static headers cannot vary per install, so a website-token keypair is UNCONFIRMED with this server — every mapped route lists 'Tiers user website plugin'.

config_fields.name: website_id
config_fields.help: Crisp website (workspace) identifier that prefixes every route (/website/{website_id}/...). Env: PLATFORM_MCP_CRISP_WEBSITE_ID.

adapter.envelope_note: Every answer is {error: boolean, reason: string, data: object|array}; failures also carry an HTTP 4xx status, which the runtime turns into isError results (the boolean `error` field is inverted relative to the runtime's ok_field envelope and is therefore not declared).
adapter.rate_note: Website tokens are 'Limited to 10,000 requests per day' plus undisclosed 'API Global' and 'API Route' limiters; plugin tokens run on a daily 'Plugin Quota'; excess answers 429 Too Many Requests or 420 Enhance Your Calm (https://docs.crisp.chat/guides/rest-api/rate-limits/, https://docs.crisp.chat/guides/rest-api/authentication/website-token/). Client bucket kept at the runtime default 2/s.

me.note: 'Resolves an existing website information' (the official curl example for both token types); account carries the envelope {error, reason, data{website_id, name, domain, logo}}.

list_inbound.note: 'Lists conversations for website' (scope website:conversation:sessions), one row per conversation: `id` = `thread_id` = session_id, `text` is 'Last message excerpt (from visitor)', `from` the visitor email (meta.email; nickname under raw.meta, unread counters under raw.unread). `page` is the page_number path segment; per_page must be 'between 20 and 50, defaults to 20' — the runtime caps `limit` at 50 but does not raise values below 20 (UNCONFIRMED how Crisp treats them). `since` is sent as filter_date_start ('date, ISO 8601, eg. 2018-03-01T17:00:00.000Z'); `channel` is not sent. updated_at / created_at are Unix ms under raw.

get_thread.note: 'Resolves messages in an existing conversation. Returns the last batch of messages if there are many messages in the conversation' (scope website:conversation:messages): there is no page-size parameter, so `limit` and `page` are ignored (older batches need timestamp_before, not sent) and `channel` is ignored. `thread_id` is the session_id; `id` is the numeric message fingerprint; `from` is the sending user id (user.user_id, 'may be operator user identifier or session identifier'; direction user/operator under raw.from); `text` is `content`, 'string if type is text or note, object if type is file, animation, audio, picker, field, carousel or event' — so non-text rows carry the content object; timestamp is Unix ms under raw.

reply.note: 'Sends a message in an existing conversation' as the operator (type text, from operator, origin chat; scope website:conversation:messages): `thread_id` is the session_id, `text` is `content` ('string if type is text'), `channel` is ignored. status is the envelope `reason`; message_id is data.fingerprint, the fingerprint Crisp assigns (UNCONFIRMED: the reference renders the response example dynamically, so the exact response body was not read).

mark_read.note: 'Marks messages as read in conversation. Either using given message fingerprints, or all messages' (scope website:conversation:messages): with from=user and origin=chat this marks all visitor chat messages of the conversation as read ('fingerprints ... if not set, this marks all messages as read in conversation'). `thread_id` is the session_id and is required; `message_id` and `channel` are not sent (fingerprints is an array the flat body map cannot express). status is the envelope `reason`.

not_offered.send: A new conversation must first be created with POST /website/{website_id}/conversation (returns the session_id) and the recipient attached with PATCH .../conversation/{session_id}/meta before a message can be posted — chained calls the adapter cannot express, and `to` (an email) has no place in the message call (https://docs.crisp.chat/references/rest-api/v1/#create-a-new-conversation, https://docs.crisp.chat/references/rest-api/v1/#send-a-message-in-conversation).

evidence: host api.crisp.chat: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (Google Trust Services)
probe: 5/5 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
HTML docs spot-check (render-doc): 5/5 tool paths found verbatim on their docs pages; every parameter and body key named on the page
